// about: Security policy for a PUBLIC upstream organisation on the GitHub Free plan. `audit --to <org>` compares the live org and repos with this file; `harden --to <org>` applies the repo-level and (with --org-level) org-level parts; `seed --to <org>` opens PRs adding the files below. Everything here is reachable with the `repo` scope except `org`, which needs `admin:org`.
name: public-upstream

org.// two_factor: Cannot be set through the API; reported by audit, applied in Settings > Authentication security.

repo.// settings: Plain repository fields (PATCH /repos). Merge hygiene: feature and seed PRs squash (title/body from the PR), sync PRs land as merge commits so both orgs keep a common ancestor, rebase is off because it rewrites history, GitHub performs the merge once reviews and checks pass (auto-merge) and deletes the head branch. `cleanup` removes branches that landed before this was on.
repo.// security: secret scanning, push protection and private vulnerability reporting are free on PUBLIC repos only; private repos are reported as n/a.
repo.// branch_protection: Applied to the default branch. Branch protection is free on public repos only. `required_linear_history` must stay false: cross-org sync lands as merge commits. `restrictions: keep` preserves whatever push restrictions a repo already has; use null to remove them or {users:[],teams:[],apps:[]} to set them. Per-repo `required_checks` in the inventory extends `required_status_checks.contexts`.

// files: Baseline files `seed` adds to every repo of the org through a PR. mode `managed` is overwritten on every seed; `create-only` is added when missing and never touched again. Templates live under `dir`; variables: name, default_branch, github_org, has_submodules, is_public, has_dockerfile, dockerfile_at_root plus `vars` (lists are space-joined).
